To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PCNA is a pivotal protein of DNA metabolism that is regulated in a cell cycle-dependent manner by cooperative and competitive binding of regulatory proteins to its trimeric ring.
the cell cycle controls the activity of DNA polymerases through the regulation of PCNA binding to the DNA template.
PCNA, a protein that plays a pivotal role in DNA replication and DNA repair, is a key player in cell cycle control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which PCNA and its associated factors regulate the cell cycle.
how the cell-cycle machinery is organized, and how the cell-cycle is controlled.
the regulation of cell-cycle events by protein-protein and protein-DNA interactions, with a focus on the cell-cycle protein proliferating cell nuclear-antigen (PCNA).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PCNA is a central component that is involved in many different aspects of DNA metabolism, including replication, repair and cell-cycle regulation, but that its precise function in these processes remains elusive.
PCNA has a central role in the coordination of the cell cycle, and that the binding of the protein to its partners is the driving force in this coordination.

PCNA has a pivotal role in cell-cycle control and that the binding of PCNA to the appropriate partners at the appropriate time and in the appropriate place is crucial for the correct execution of the cell cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cell uses a variety of proteins to regulate the activity of PCNAs.
the PCNA ring structure is a central hub for cell-cycle regulation.
PCNA is a central player in the regulation and coordination of DNA replication and repair.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PCNA has a key role in the coordination of cell-cycle transitions and in cell-cycle checkpoints.
competition for PCNA binding is a key mechanism for cell-cycle control.
the cell-cycle changes that occur in the cell are not only driven by the cell cycle itself, but also by the interactions of the cell cycle with the cell-cycle machinery.
